subject: HealthNexus — data territory handshake, DPA addendum & procurement timing
body:
Message 1/5
From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@healthnexus.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthnexus.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA addendum — region anchoring & temporary cross-region processing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput profile looks promising. Before Procurement will sign the MSA/DPA, our legal and security teams need clarity on two operational items:

1) Region anchoring: HealthNexus requires primary residency in the US for customer data and a commitment that processing will be pinned to the US region unless a documented failover/fallback is triggered. We understand temporary, scheduled cross-region processing (e.g., for patching or short-lived replication) may be necessary; we need a clear SLA window and notification workflow.

2) Subprocessor roster & temporary hops: please provide the active subprocessor list, and confirm which subprocessors might see transient cross-region traffic (if any). For any transient reprocessing, we need a 72-hour maximum window and notification to our security mailbox.

Can you also share the proposed DPA addendum language or an example playbook outlining operational steps? Procurement is aiming to complete signature in the next two weeks, contingent on these items.

Best,
Emma Clarke
Head of Security Programs
HealthNexus

---

Message 2/5
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@healthnexus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum — region anchoring & temporary cross-region processing

Emma — thanks for the clear asks and for outlining Procurement timing. Quick summary and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Region anchoring: we can commit to primary US residency for HealthNexus workloads and will include an anchoring clause in the DPA addendum.
- Temporary cross-region processing: Redwood permits transient reprocessing for operational reasons (patching, incident failover, telemetry backfills) with a default max window of 72 hours; any exception beyond that requires written approval.
- Notifications: we will provide automated incident/notification hooks and an ops-runbook that triggers e-mail to security@healthnexus.com and creates a tracked ticket in your SSO/ITSM via webhook.

I've attached a first-pass playbook (data-residency-playbook-v1.pdf) and our up-to-date subprocessor roster (subprocessor-roster-20270518.csv). The playbook contains the proposed operational SLA language and the failover approval flow.

Next: Marissa (legal) — can you review the addendum language below and, separately, confirm whether we should propose the 72-hour cap in the DPA itself or as an operational annex that teams can amend? Laura — ops, can you confirm the notification/webhook cadence and whether we can provide a 24-hour notice for planned maintenance windows that may cause transient hops?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

Message 3/5
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@healthnexus.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum — region anchoring & temporary cross-region processing

Karthik / Emma — looping in language suggestions. High level: we should capture the 72-hour transient processing cap in the DPA addendum as a default operational guarantee, with an explicit process for written exceptions. That keeps the commitment contractually clear while allowing customers to request longer windows (e.g., for long-running data migrations) under negotiated terms.

Suggested clause (draft):
"Region Anchoring and Temporary Processing: Provider shall ensure that Customer data is processed and stored primarily in the agreed region (United States). Temporary cross-region processing for operational reasons (including but not limited to failover, patching, and scheduled replication) shall be limited to a maximum duration of 72 consecutive hours unless Customer and Provider agree in writing to an alternate window. Provider will notify Customer's security contact and create a tracked incident within two hours of cross-region processing commencement and provide a closure summary upon completion."

Emma — if that flows for you, we'll incorporate into the DPA addendum and send a DocuSign link that references the existing MSA. Also note: the subprocessor roster includes two cloud-edge partners that operate an EU-based analytics cache; those partners will not receive HealthNexus customer payloads unless a transient replication event is invoked under the clause above.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

---

Message 4/5
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@healthnexus.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum — region anchoring & temporary cross-region processing

Emma — operational confirmations below:
- Notification cadence: for planned maintenance that may cause transient cross-region hops we can provide a 24-hour advance notification. For unplanned failovers we will open a tracked incident and send an initial notification within two hours of the event starting, as Marissa's draft states.
- Telemetry & evidence: we can provide an ops snapshot (time-stamped routing table + KV cache copy note) and an end-of-event summary. We will keep these artifacts for 90 days by default and produce them for audits per the DPA.
- Subprocessor visibility: the roster includes the two edge analytics vendors (names in the attached CSV). Those vendors process anonymized telemetry only unless Customer explicitly requests analytics features that require payload-level processing; that flow will be separately scoped and require a written addendum.

Olga — please confirm the internal runbook step that ties a 'transient processing' incident to a compliance approval ticket. If that is in place, we can push the addendum for signature.

Thanks — Laura
Head of Reliability Operations
Redwood Inference

---

Message 5/5
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@healthnexus.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA addendum — region anchoring & temporary cross-region processing

Confirmed: the runbook already ties transient-processing events to a compliance-approval ticket and requires a 2-step ops + privacy signoff for any extension beyond 72 hours. We have a canned webhook to create a ticket in the customer's ITSM and a templated notification e-mail for closure.

Emma — we're ready to formalize. Next steps I propose:
- We'll incorporate Marissa's clause into a DPA addendum and generate a DocuSign envelope targeted at your Procurement address.
- Karthik — please attach the two files we sent (playbook + roster) to the DocuSign envelope and include the SOW name/Deal ID.
- Emma / Procurement — please confirm DocuSign recipients. Once we have signers confirmed, Procurement can complete the DocuSign flow within 48 hours and we can schedule a short ops handshake to validate webhook receipts.

Olga Petrov
Privacy & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

--
